title: Calgary Sun
article: A Calgary police officer has told a fatality inquiry that the woman he arrested was so drunk that he was afraid to leave her alone.
Const. David Bailey says he was so concerned 53-year-old Eva Farnel might choke to death that he charged her with breaching the peace and took her into custody.
Farnel later used her shirt to strangle herself in a jail cell.

Bailey says that after he removed Farnel from her residence on May 8, 2006, he decided to charge a still belligerent Farnel with being intoxicated in public to avoid her facing the stigma of a criminal charge.
Farnel family lawyer Murray Stone suggested she was only in public because Bailey removed her unwillingly from her home.
Stone said that medically, Farnel was 'fine.'
'She's not going to die, she's just going to wake up wishing she had,' Stone told the inquiry on Monday.
Bailey told inquiry counsel Sean McDonough he went to Farnel's apartment at 4:30 a.m. in response to a noise complaint \_ the second there that night.
He found an extremely intoxicated Farnel sitting in her living room babbling incoherently, her neck muscles unable to hold her head in place.
Paramedics were brought in to examine her, but found nothing to justify her hospitalization, Bailey said.
'I remember thinking 'I have no option but to take her down to arrest processing,' he said.
'She needed to be monitored and taken to a place of safety.'
Homicide Det. Chris Matthews said he viewed videotape of Farnel in her cell and noted she removed her shirt at 9:15 a.m. and immediately turned it into a ligature.
She was found unconscious nine minutes later.
The inquiry, which can't find blame, continues Tuesday.
